questionText:
Consider the C code fragment given below.

Assuming that $m$ and $n$ point to valid NULL-terminated linked lists, invocation of join will
options: append list $m$ to the end of list $n$ for all inputs.
either cause a null pointer dereference or append list $m$ to the end of list $n$.
cause a null pointer dereference for all inputs.
append list $n$ to the end of list $m$ for all inputs.
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze function behavior for non-empty list $n$.
If list $n$ is not empty ($n \neq \text{NULL}$), $p$ is initialized to point to the head of list $n$. The while loop traverses until $p$ points to the last node of list $n$ (where $p \rightarrow \text{next} == \text{NULL}$). The line $p \rightarrow \text{next} = m$ then links the last node of list $n$ to list $m$, appending list $m$ to the end of list $n$.

Step 2: Analyze edge case for empty list $n$.
If list $n$ is empty ($n == \text{NULL}$), $p$ becomes $\text{NULL}$. Evaluating $p \rightarrow \text{next}$ inside the while loop condition attempts to access memory through a null pointer, causing a null pointer dereference.

Conclusion:
The code will either cause a null pointer dereference (when list $n$ is empty) or successfully append list $m$ to the end of list $n$. Hence, option (B) is correct.
